bug_semantics: The authenticated GlassFish Administration Console endpoint /shared/instanceStatus.jsf copies the attacker-controlled GET parameter instanceName into pageSession.instanceName and then emits it inside an f:verbatim HTML attribute, <span class="instance-name" data-instancename="#{pageSession.instanceName}"/>. Because that verbatim attribute context does not HTML-encode quotes, a link containing instanceName=%22%20id=%22x%22%20tabindex=%221%22%20onfocus=%22alert(1)%22%20autofocus=%22 breaks out of data-instancename and installs an autofocus/onfocus handler. A remote attacker can send that link to an already authenticated console user and execute script in the Administration Console origin, permitting actions or data access in the victim's session.
flaw_origin: Commit e0e163690c621208605120d924b8779ce5a23f7a created appserver/admingui/cluster/src/main/resources/shared/instanceStatus.jsf and in the same atomic asynchronous-status feature added both getRequestValue(key="instanceName" value="#{pageSession.instanceName}") and the unescaped f:verbatim data-instancename sink at original line 37. It also added callers in clusters.jsf, nodes.jsf, and instancesTable.inc. git log -L 37,37 and git log -S 'data-instancename="#{pageSession.instanceName}"' each identify only e0e163690c621208605120d924b8779ce5a23f7a. This is a one-parent, non-merge feature commit, not a move, refactor, revert, release commit, or squash aggregate.

evidence: First-party report https://gitlab.eclipse.org/security/vulnerability-reports/-/work_items/226 names affected endpoint /shared/instanceStatus.jsf, GET parameter instanceName, authenticated-console victim prerequisite, and the quote/onfocus/autofocus payload; its public API object (GET /api/v4/projects/3804/issues/226) remains opened, labels vulnerability::confirmed and status::awaiting_release. Bundle/GitHub advisory GHSA-vqrm-83g6-pfv4 records console-common and console-cluster-plugin vulnerable <=7.0.25 and first_patched_version null. In the validated clone, reproduce the BIC with: git show e0e163690c621208605120d924b8779ce5a23f7a -- appserver/admingui/cluster/src/main/resources/shared/instanceStatus.jsf; git log origin/main -L 37,37:appserver/admingui/cluster/src/main/resources/shared/instanceStatus.jsf; and git log --all -S'data-instancename="#{pageSession.instanceName}"' -- that path. Direct parent absence is reproducible with git ls-tree -r --name-only 28b915e73f2839fd2f5d62ee22b4d204a1a432b8 -- appserver/admingui/cluster/src/main/resources/shared/instanceStatus.jsf, which returns no path because the endpoint did not exist. git tag --contains e0e163690c621208605120d924b8779ce5a23f7a starts at 7.0.5; git show -s 7.0.4 7.0.5 resolves release commits 0dd0bbdcf0d1c711e8c226a01a1b8ed7f951c06f and 7b49f4eaf669e9a3b4f4648254f9016872455236 respectively, establishing source absence through 7.0.4 and presence from 7.0.5 (the reporter demonstrated 7.0.15). No direct source fix exists: git log --all --follow for instanceStatus.jsf contains only the BIC, and git rev-parse of that path at the BIC, 7.0.25, 7.0.26, 7.1.1, 8.0.4, and origin/main returns the identical blob f92b2ab6ffdff00a6eb43e39f6b4c2d09ec54ecd each time. Thus public history supplies no closing fix SHA or patched source boundary. Finally, git cat-file -p e0e163690c621208605120d924b8779ce5a23f7a gives parent 28b915e73f2839fd2f5d62ee22b4d204a1a432b8, the human author/committer identities, and the complete marker-free message quoted in ai_marker.
reasoning: The vulnerable request-to-verbatim-attribute flow first appears as newly written code in the atomic e0e163690c621208605120d924b8779ce5a23f7a feature commit, and its immediate parent lacks even the endpoint, so it is the smallest true BIC. Release ancestry places that source change after 7.0.4 and in 7.0.5 onward; the public report's 7.0.15 is a demonstrated affected release, while GHSA's package range extends through 7.0.25 without naming a patched version. The exact vulnerable file remains byte-identical in later public tags and main, so no direct closing fix can honestly be assigned. AI judgment is nevertheless closed because the protocol permits explicit unpatched cases and requires BIC-only commit-object evidence: that object is authored and committed by a named human and contains only a human Signed-off-by trailer, with no AI marker. Therefore the appropriate verdict is NOT_AI.
remaining_gap: unpatched: no upstream commit in the validated public GlassFish history removes, validates, or contextually encodes the instanceName f:verbatim attribute sink, and the advisory names no first patched version; consequently fix_sha and direct_fix_sha are null and there is no fixed release boundary to report.
